title: Terrace Water Line
premise: A long farming drama under emerald terraces and silver morning-mist lines. Xiao Zhou and A-Xiang are easily confused by looks; the waterwheel spine goes intact→broken-teeth→repaired with new teeth; after the ox cart Green-Seedling wrecks it must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_watcher: Uncle Ridge in his fifties, short gray hair, dark-green straw cape and coarse trousers, bamboo water gauge at the waist, calves caked in mud, steady eyes.
states.waist_wound_cane: The same Uncle Ridge after a waist injury: hard to bend, walking slowly on a yellow-rattan cane, still in that faded dark-green straw cape.
states.deceased: Uncle Ridge has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the field-hut narrow couch, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_farmer: Young Xiao Zhou: a lean transplanting apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, cyan-green headscarf, gray-brown short jacket, straw-braid wrist rope on the left, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult Xiao Zhou: a broad-shouldered water watcher in his twenties, still wearing the cyan-green headscarf and left-wrist straw rope, steady expression.

states.intact_turning: A wooden waterwheel spine standing by the ridge, paddles intact, clear water line flowing in the spine trough, creaking as it turns.
states.teeth_jammed: The same waterwheel spine: paddles with broken teeth jammed, spine trough dry, axle skewed.
states.teeth_replaced: After new paddles, the waterwheel spine turns again; new-wood patches remain on the spine, distinct from the first intact state.

states.intact: An oil-paper-covered water-log book, cover lettered 'South Slope Nine Mounds', pages filled in brush with sluice times and water levels.
states.mud_stained: The same water-log book soaked through with field mud water, cover warped and wrinkled, writing smeared into mud blotches.

states.intact: A green-lacquered two-wheeled ox cart, white letters 'Green-Seedling' on the sides, straw-lined bed for hauling seedlings.
states.ridge_overturned: The green-lacquer ox cart overturned on the ridge, sides split, straw scattered—wreckage that can no longer haul seedlings.

states.young_visitor: Young A-Xiang: face nearly identical to Xiao Zhou's, but turmeric-yellow headscarf, bamboo-joint bracelet on the right wrist, more playful look.
states.adult_mat_weaver: Adult A-Xiang: face nearly identical to adult Xiao Zhou's, still turmeric-yellow headscarf and bamboo-joint bracelet, reed-mat roll on the shoulder.

segments.action: At dusk Uncle Ridge climbs to the South-slope water shed; the waterwheel spine creaks turning water by the ridge.
A row of five oil-paper lanterns hangs under the South-slope water shed eaves; Uncle Ridge polishes each shade.
Two sluice-opening gongs hang under the water-shed beam; Uncle Ridge reaches up and lets the faces tremble lightly.
Uncle Ridge circles the waterwheel spine, checking paddles and whether the spine trough runs clear.
From the shed mouth Uncle Ridge watches the sky beyond the layered terraces.
The intact waterwheel spine quietly turns a clear water line beside the Nine-mound ridges.
Uncle Ridge sits on a bamboo chair and dozes by the oil-paper lanterns.
Night mist climbs the ridge; Uncle Ridge tightens the collar of his dark-green straw cape.
Uncle Ridge opens the water-log book and brush-notes that night's sluice time.
Uncle Ridge draws a water-level curve in the water-log book.
Uncle Ridge closes the water-log book and sets it back in the shed's clay jar.
Water-glimmer from the waterwheel spine sweeps Uncle Ridge's cheek.
Uncle Ridge gently wipes mud flecks from the bamboo water gauges with a cloth.
On the morning Nine-mound ridges, Uncle Ridge greets young Xiao Zhou driving the green-lacquer Green-Seedling.
Xiao Zhou steadies Green-Seedling and lifts seedling bundles from the bed to the paddy edge.
Uncle Ridge points to the three bamboo water gauges by the water mouth and teaches Xiao Zhou to read the marks.
Xiao Zhou squats on the mud ridge and curiously touches the water mirrors in the morning mist.
Uncle Ridge points to the valley and explains the pumping order to Xiao Zhou.
Xiao Zhou looks back at parked Green-Seedling, eyes full of longing.
They lean side by side on a ridge stone post, listening to the waterwheel creak.
In the granary dark lane, A-Xiang with the turmeric-yellow headscarf turns from behind a grain bin.

segments.action: Seasons turn; day after day Uncle Ridge climbs to the South-slope water shed.
Another snowy night Uncle Ridge wraps his cape tight and keeps watch by the waterwheel spine.
At spring-planting sluice open, Uncle Ridge checks mound numbers inside the shed.
At high-summer noon Uncle Ridge wipes the sun-hot bamboo rail outside the shed.
Autumn rain falls on end; the waterwheel spine's water line goes white in the fog.
Another New Year's Eve Uncle Ridge keeps vigil alone in the South-slope water shed till dawn.
On the eve of grain-drying Uncle Ridge clears the water mouth two hours early.
On a full-moon night Uncle Ridge tops oil in every oil-paper lantern.
When a cold snap hits Uncle Ridge hangs wind-break grass curtains on the shed door.
Around Qingming Uncle Ridge sweeps leaves and gravel from the Nine-mound ridges.
In plum-rain season Uncle Ridge repeatedly checks ridge seepage.
For three rainless nights straight Uncle Ridge pins sluice times dead tight.
One night the level drops sharply; Uncle Ridge has to open a side ditch.
The waterwheel hesitates; Uncle Ridge quickly checks the paddles.
At three in the morning Uncle Ridge drinks ice-cold tea from a coarse porcelain bowl.
Inside the shed he sorts the bamboo water gauge numbers.
The sluice-opening gongs tremble lightly in the wind; Uncle Ridge looks up to listen.
When the sky pales Uncle Ridge notes the last sluice of the night.
Before leaving the shed he glances once more at the waterwheel spine's intact paddles.
At dawn Uncle Ridge patrols the Nine-mound ridges; green-lacquer Green-Seedling sits by a stone post.
Uncle Ridge crouches to check Green-Seedling's wheels and straw pad.
Uncle Ridge walks to the water mouth; those earlier three bamboo water gauges still stand neatly stuck.
A strange earth-yellow flat cart rolls the ridge road—manure in the bed, not Green-Seedling.
Uncle Ridge stands on the mud ridge noting last night's peak water level.
Uncle Ridge replants the bird-scare crow figure upright.
Far morning mist withdraws, revealing deeper valley shadow.
Mountain flood surges; the South-slope water shed trembles in the water roar; the waterwheel spine shakes hard.
Turbid flow scours the ridge; Uncle Ridge rushes to the floodgate plank.
With a dull crack the waterwheel spine paddles jam on broken teeth; the axle skews.

segments.action: An orange-red Iron-Ox seedling tractor climbs the Nine-mound ridges—nothing like the overturned Green-Seedling.
Water officer Old Qin steps onto the ridge and talks beside Uncle Ridge; the two builds are close.
Old Qin points at the Iron-Ox seedling tractor and explains the new water-delivery roster to Uncle Ridge.
The Iron-Ox seedling tractor drives off; Uncle Ridge alone watches it leave the ridge.
Wind flaps the roster sheet Old Qin left behind.
Outside the granary comes neighboring-mound youth Daosui in a cyan-green headscarf; at a glance he somewhat resembles young Xiao Zhou.
Daosui tries transplanting, but Uncle Ridge shakes his head—he is not Xiao Zhou after all.
Daosui leaves the Nine-mound ridges with an empty seedling basket; his back fades on the ridge road.
Years later at dusk, hard-to-bend Uncle Ridge leans on a yellow-rattan cane outside the South-slope water shed.
